simple: every read and write touches only memory the program may touch, and only while it is valid.
analogy: writing only inside your own boxes on the slate, and only while the slate is yours.
precise: the property that a program has no out-of-bounds access, no use of freed or uninitialised memory and no type-confused access; C and C++ do not guarantee it.
source: D1 of F11-07 (C++ Core Guidelines) — title only, pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a number grows past the biggest its type can hold and wraps to a small one.
analogy: a three-digit tally rolling from 999 back to 000.
precise: an arithmetic result outside the representable range of the type; unsigned wraps modulo 2^n, signed is undefined behaviour. A size computed this way can be far too small.
source: D3 of F11-07 (C++ working draft), R5 of F11-07 (lab run) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: an input crafted so that a bug does something useful for an attacker.
analogy: a name chosen precisely so the overflow lands on the "let in" box.
precise: an input or sequence of inputs that drives a vulnerability to a goal — changing data, redirecting control flow or leaking memory — rather than merely crashing.
source: D1 of F11-07 (C++ Core Guidelines) — title only, pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: overwriting a value the processor will load into the instruction pointer, so the attacker chooses what runs next.
analogy: the castle guard now follows the attacker's written orders.
precise: corrupting a saved return address, function pointer or virtual-table pointer so that a later transfer of control jumps to an attacker-chosen address.
source: D5 of F11-07 (Intel SDM Vol. 1/3) — title only, pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the first and last valid positions of an array or buffer.
analogy: the top and bottom lines of a ledger page.
precise: the half-open range [0, size) of valid indices of a contiguous object; an access outside it is undefined behaviour in C++.
source: D1 of F11-08 (C++ working draft) — title only, pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the time between when an object is created and when it is destroyed.
analogy: while the page belongs to this ledger.
precise: the interval from completion of an object's constructor (or allocation of its storage) to the start of its destructor (or release of its storage); access outside it is undefined.
source: D1 of F11-08 (C++ working draft) — title only, pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: whose job it is to free a resource.
analogy: the one clerk who may tear out a page.
precise: the responsibility for releasing a resource exactly once, expressed in C++ by the type that holds it (a value, a unique_ptr, a shared_ptr), not by convention.
source: D2 of F11-08 (A Tour of C++) — title only, pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: tie a resource to an object so it is freed when the object goes out of scope.
analogy: the page is torn out automatically when its folder is closed.
precise: Resource Acquisition Is Initialisation — acquire in the constructor, release in the destructor, so every path (including exceptions) releases exactly once.
source: D2 of F11-08 (A Tour of C++) — title only, pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a pointer to something that no longer exists.
analogy: a bookmark in a page that has been torn out.
precise: a pointer, reference, iterator or view whose referent's lifetime has ended; using it is undefined behaviour and a frequent root of use-after-free.
source: D1 of F11-08 (C++ working draft), R2 of F11-08 (lab run) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a fuzzer that keeps inputs which make the program run new code.
analogy: keeping any document that makes the clerk open a drawer never opened before.
precise: fuzzing that measures which control-flow edges each input exercises and adds inputs reaching new edges to the corpus, steering mutation toward unexplored code.
source: D1 of F11-09 (libFuzzer/AFL docs), R6 of F11-09 (the lab fuzzer) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the set of interesting inputs the fuzzer keeps and mutates.
analogy: the stack of documents worth copying and altering again.
precise: the collection of seed inputs plus every input retained for reaching new coverage; mutations are drawn from it.
source: D1 of F11-09 (libFuzzer/AFL docs) — title only, pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a table that records which jumps in the code have run.
analogy: a checklist of every drawer in the office, ticked when opened.
precise: an array indexed by a hash of each control-flow edge; the compiler's -fsanitize-coverage instrumentation sets an entry when that edge executes.
source: D2 of F11-09 (Clang SanitizerCoverage), R6 of F11-09 — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: shrinking a crashing input to the smallest that still crashes.
analogy: trimming the document to the few marks that trip the clerk.
precise: delta debugging — repeatedly removing parts of the input, keeping any removal that preserves the crash — to produce a small, readable reproducer.
source: D1 of F11-09 (libFuzzer/AFL docs), R4 and R9 of F11-09 (lab runs) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a secret value placed between a buffer and the saved return address, checked before returning.
analogy: a wax seal that breaks if the clerk writes too far.
precise: a random value (__stack_chk_guard) the compiler stores on the stack with -fstack-protector; the function checks it before returning and aborts via __stack_chk_fail if it changed.
source: D1 of F11-10 (GCC options), R1 of F11-10 (lab run) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: memory is either writable or executable, never both; data pages cannot run as code.
analogy: guards never act on notes written in visitors' notebooks.
precise: the no-execute page bit (x86-64 XD bit 63, honoured when EFER.NXE is set); an instruction fetch from a non-executable page faults. W^X never maps a page writable and executable at once.
source: D2 of F11-10 (Intel SDM Vol. 3), R3 of F11-10 (lab run) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the program's stack, heap and code sit at different addresses each run.
analogy: the rooms are rearranged every night.
precise: Address Space Layout Randomisation — the kernel loads the stack, heap, libraries and (for a PIE) the program itself at randomised bases, so an attacker cannot know a target address in advance.
source: D3 of F11-10 (Linux ASLR docs), R4 of F11-10 (lab run) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a program built so it can be loaded at any address.
analogy: a building with no fixed street number.
precise: a Position-Independent Executable (ELF type ET_DYN) whose code uses relative addressing, letting the loader place it at a random base — the prerequisite for ASLR of the main program.
source: D4 of F11-10 (System V ABI), R5 of F11-10 (lab run) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a written set of rules for how code must be written, so dangerous constructs are avoided or flagged.
analogy: the guards' checklist that every order must satisfy.
precise: a documented rule set (here the SEI CERT C++ standard and the C++ Core Guidelines) with rationale and, where possible, automated enforcement.
source: D1 of F11-11 (CERT C++, Core Guidelines) — title only, pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: checking code for mistakes without running it.
analogy: a second guard reading the order before it is acted on.
precise: tools (here clang-tidy) that inspect source or the compiler's representation to find rule violations and likely bugs, reporting file, line and rule name.
source: D2 of F11-11 (clang-tidy docs), R1 of F11-11 (lab run) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: make the build fail on any compiler warning.
analogy: refusing an order that has any crossing-out, not filing it anyway.
precise: the -Werror option, usually with a chosen warning set (-Wall -Wextra -Wconversion ...), so a warning stops the build and must be fixed.
source: D3 of F11-11 (GCC warning options), R3 of F11-11 (lab run) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: putting a value into a type too small or of the wrong sign, silently changing it.
analogy: copying a four-digit number into a three-box field.
precise: an implicit conversion that may lose value or change sign (e.g. uint32_t to short); flagged by -Wconversion / -Wsign-conversion.
source: D3 of F11-11 (GCC warning options), R3 of F11-11 (lab run) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a tool that flags suspicious or non-conforming code.
analogy: the colleague who points at the smudge before you hand the order over.
precise: a static-analysis tool with configurable check sets (clang-tidy groups cert-*, bugprone-*, clang-analyzer-*) run in the editor and in CI.
source: D2 of F11-11 (clang-tidy docs) — title only, pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a system that builds and checks every change automatically.
analogy: the gate that no order reaches without passing the checklist.
precise: an automated pipeline that, on each change, compiles with warnings-as-errors, runs the analyser, the tests under sanitizers and a short fuzzing pass, failing the change if any step fails.
source: D1 of F11-11 (CERT C++, Core Guidelines) — title only, pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: data from outside your program that an attacker might control.
analogy: paperwork written by whoever sent the crate.
precise: any value crossing a trust boundary — a file, network packet, device register or descriptor, user-space pointer — that must be validated before use because its source is not under your control.
source: D1 of F11-12 (curriculum 5.4 Trust row, a map to sources AH-4) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the line between code you control and data you do not.
analogy: the castle gate, where outside paperwork meets inside rules.
precise: the interface at which data of lower trust enters a higher-trust component; all validation must happen on the inside of it, once, before the data is used.
source: D1 of F11-12 (curriculum 5.4 Trust row) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a small record a device gives describing itself or its data.
analogy: the crate's paperwork.
precise: a device-supplied structure (e.g. a USB configuration descriptor with a wTotalLength, or a DMA descriptor with address and length fields) whose every field is attacker-influenceable and must be bounded.
source: D2 of F11-12 (USB specification) — title only, pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a device reading or writing memory directly, without the CPU copying each byte.
analogy: a courier allowed into the storeroom to fetch goods himself.
precise: Direct Memory Access — a device transfers data to or from memory over the bus; a malicious or buggy device can read or overwrite memory it was not meant to unless constrained by an IOMMU.
source: D3 of F11-12 (Linux IOMMU/DMA docs) — title only, pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: when input is invalid, reject it and stop, rather than guessing.
analogy: refuse the crate whose paperwork does not match, do not unpack it anyway.
precise: a design in which an unexpected or malformed input leads to a safe refusal (error returned, operation aborted), never to undefined behaviour or a best-effort continue.
source: D1 of F11-12 (curriculum 5.4 Trust row) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
